citation: Kaslow et al. (2015), Developing a CubeSat Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) Reference Model - Interim status
title: Developing a CubeSat Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) Reference Model - Interim status
modeling_scope: Generic CubeSat Reference Model and CubeSat Project Model covering space and ground systems, stakeholders, mission needs/objectives/measures of effectiveness/constraints, requirements flowdown, lifecycle domains, operations phases, external environments and constraints, and logical/physical architectures down to subsystem level. EPS/power is included as a generic bus subsystem with components, and prior RAX phases modeled solar energy collection, subsystem power consumption, energy storage/usage, and energy trade studies. Verification/testing is modeled generally, not as a detailed EPS-specific procedure.
mbse_language_method_tool: SysML using OOSEM; No Magic MagicDraw as the graphical SysML tool. Prior phases used MagicDraw, Cameo Simulation Toolkit, ModelCenter, MBSE Analyzer, STK, ParaMagic, SLIM, and MATLAB to interface SysML with modeling and simulation tools.
robot_platform: CubeSat/nanosatellite spacecraft platform; generic CubeSat Reference/Project Model, with prior application to RAX, a three-unit CubeSat, and planned validation on a hypothetical CirrusSat mission.
task_domain: CubeSat mission and system design/development across the lifecycle, including space-ground mission architecture, operations, power/energy, communications/link analysis, data collection/storage/download, and regulatory/testing constraints.
interface: SysML model integration with discipline-specific engineering models and COTS modeling/simulation tools; model also identifies space-ground, launch service, communication service, and payload-bus interfaces. No detailed human interface is reported.
feedback: Prior RAX simulations time-stepped scenarios, sent signals, updated state values, and supported trade studies by varying solar panel area, battery capacity, orbital altitude, and ground station network. The current model is planned for controlled roll-out and update based on user feedback; no closed EPS verification feedback loop is specified.
evaluation: Interim status paper demonstrated the reference/project model with SysML diagrams, subsystem tables, and summaries of prior RAX simulations and trade studies. The current reference model had not yet been validated; validation by applying it to a hypothetical CirrusSat mission and roll-out to workshops/courses/programs were stated as next steps.
rq_relevance: RQ1: yes for system-level CubeSat MBSE reference modeling, with EPS/power included generically as a bus subsystem and through earlier power/energy simulation examples. RQ2: partial because MBSE/modeling outcomes are claimed for integration, consistency, reuse as a starting point, trade studies, and mission-assurance artifacts, but explicit EPS reliability or reproducibility outcomes are not reported. RQ3: partial because general verification/validation/testing/reporting elements are to be represented in the reference/project model, but no EPS-specific verification procedure is detailed.
claimed_outcomes: Integrability: MBSE is claimed to help integrate discipline-specific engineering models and simulations, and past phases showed SysML can interface with special-purpose M&S tools.

Consistency/traceability: the system model is claimed to provide a cohesive and consistent source of system requirements, design analysis, and verification, with requirements flowdown from mission need to subsystem requirements.
Reuse/customization: the CubeSat Reference Model and Project Model are intended as starting points for mission-specific CubeSat models, with teams able to modify, add, and remove SysML elements.
Mission assurance support: systems engineering artifacts can be extracted from the model to demonstrate mission assurance to stakeholders.
Analysis/trade-study support: prior RAX modeling supported power, communications, data-download, energy storage, solar-panel, battery-capacity, altitude, and ground-station trade studies.
No explicit reliability or reproducibility outcome for EPS modeling is reported.
verification_validation_linkage: The paper links the reference model to SysML elements for requirements, design, analysis, verification, and validation. Cal Poly CubeSat Design Specification items for testing and verification reporting/signoff are to be populated into the Project Model as Activity or Sequence diagrams. This is general CubeSat/project V&V linkage; EPS-specific verification procedures are not reported.
key_findings: The paper reports the fourth phase of the INCOSE SSWG CubeSat Challenge, aiming to build a generic CubeSat Reference Model and a CubeSat Project Model for mission-specific reuse.

The modeling approach uses SysML and OOSEM, with MagicDraw and interfaces to COTS simulation tools; SysML diagrams cover requirements, structures, behaviors, and parametrics from system to component level.

The model covers the full CubeSat lifecycle and operational phases, with stakeholder needs, objectives, measures of effectiveness, constraints, and requirements flowdown represented before subsystem-level architecture is detailed.

Power/EPS is present as a logical bus subsystem and generic component set; earlier RAX work modeled solar energy collection, subsystem power consumption, energy collection/usage, and energy-level trade studies.
Verification is addressed at the general model/project level through V&V SysML elements and planned testing/verification reporting diagrams, but there is no detailed EPS-specific verification model.

The current model was still interim: nomenclature, stakeholder information, and logical architecture had been established, while lifecycle-specific model definition, concept/development models, validation, and broader roll-out remained future work.
limitations_gaps: The Phase 2 RAX model lacked the ability to time-step through a behavioral model and determine whether requirements were satisfied throughout the entire RAX mission.
Assessment of MBSE methodologies and a survey of MBSE tools were stated as beyond the scope of the survey/material discussed.

At the interim stage, work had focused on nomenclature, stakeholders, needs/objectives/measures of effectiveness, and architecture down to logical subsystems; lifecycle-stage model depth and concept/development phase models remained next steps.
Validation by applying the model to a hypothetical CirrusSat mission and updating it after roll-out feedback were future work, not completed evaluation results.
No formal threats-to-validity section is provided, and no EPS-specific verification procedure or EPS reliability/reproducibility outcome is reported.

quality.rationale: IEEE Aerospace Conference paper with DOI. The paper acknowledges interim status, previous modeling shortcomings, beyond-scope items, and next steps, but it does not provide a formal limitations or threats-to-validity discussion.

evidence_quotes.quote: MBSE creates a system model that helps integrate other discipline specific engineering models and simulations. The system level model is initiated at the start of a project and evolves throughout development. It provides a cohesive and consistent source of system requirements, design analysis, and verification.

evidence_quotes.claim: SysML scope from system to component level
evidence_quotes.quote: SysML diagrams are used to describe requirements, structures, behaviors, and parametrics from the system down to the component level.

evidence_quotes.claim: Reference model intended for reuse by CubeSat projects
evidence_quotes.quote: Develop a CubeSat Reference Model that other projects can use as a starting point for their mission specific CubeSat model.
Develop a CubeSat Project Model that models how CubeSat design and development are to be accomplished.

evidence_quotes.claim: Power/EPS modeling in prior RAX phase
evidence_quotes.quote: Power: Solar energy collection and subsystem power consumption taking into account mission activities and states.

evidence_quotes.claim: Prior limitation of behavior/time-step verification capability
evidence_quotes.quote: lacked the ability to time-step through a behavioral model and determine whether requirements were satisfied throughout the entire RAX mission.
A new model was developed with the capability to time-step through a scenario and to capture the energy collection and usage processes as well as data collection, storage, and download.
On-board energy level as a function of solar panel area and maximum battery capacity.
The past phases have demonstrated that it is possible to interface SysML with special purpose M&S tools in order to model a space mission and carry out trades studies.

evidence_quotes.claim: General V&V elements in reference model
evidence_quotes.quote: The reference model contains SysML elements for the requirements, design, analysis, verification, and validation activities.

evidence_quotes.claim: Testing and verification reporting represented in project model
evidence_quotes.quote: requirements covering communication licenses, remote sensing licenses, debris mitigation, testing, and verification reporting/signoff, which will be populated into the Project Model as Activity diagrams or Sequence diagrams.
evidence_quotes.location: Section 3, Cal Poly CubeSat Design Specification

evidence_quotes.quote: The power components for CubeSats include solar panels, batteries, regulators, and wiring harnesses.
Power: Monitor, collect, store, distribute, and control spacecraft power.

The effort to date has been focused on establishing nomenclature; incorporating the stakeholders and their needs, objectives, and measures of effectiveness; and defining the architecture down to the logical subsystems.
The model will be validated by applying it to a hypothetical CirrusSat mission to detect cirrus clouds.
